title: 3. Teaching content (source-backed)
objective: Study-guide review — Study Guide — Session 1: Agentic AI for Dev & IT Ops in Banking: 3. Teaching content (source-backed).

blocks.text: A. Hook — from autocomplete to agent (09:00–09:08)

Teaching prose (Thai delivery): เปิดด้วยความจริงที่ห้องสัมผัสได้ — ทุกคนเคยใช้ autocomplete / code-completion มาแล้ว นั่นคือ "AI ที่เติมโค้ดให้ทีละบรรทัด" แต่ agentic AI ไปไกลกว่านั้น มันไม่ได้เดาบรรทัดถัดไป มัน รับโจทย์ → วางแผน → เรียกเครื่องมือ → ลงมือทำ → ตรวจผล เหมือนมี junior engineer ที่ทำงานเร็วมาก แต่ "ต้องมีคนเซ็นอนุมัติ" เสมอ. ในธนาคารเราสนใจสองอย่างพร้อมกัน: เร็วขึ้น และ คุมได้ / ตรวจสอบย้อนได้. [DESIGN-S1 §A]
Slide key points (English):

items: Autocomplete suggests the next line. An agent completes the whole task. The jump is agency, not magic. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:00]
Agentic AI = reason → plan → use tools → execute → verify — a loop, not one shot. [DESIGN-S1 §A]
Banking lens: speed is worthless without control + auditability. [DESIGN-S1 §A] [SCOPE: Hard constraints]
Today: watch one agent fix a real bug — then see exactly where a human must stay in the loop. [DESIGN-S1 §A]

blocks.text: Defender-lens (mandatory spoken aside, ~20s, whole room): "Look at these four as a defender, not a developer. Reason and plan — you cannot make those repeatable; the agent's judgment changes run to run. Tool-use and execute — that's the only place a human or a gate can stand. So your whole job today is: watch the two you can't control, and put your controls on the two you can." This gives the non-coding SOC/blue-team learner a stake from minute 8. [ROS-1.2 §S1 SAY-ALOUD #1]
B. The four capabilities — what "agentic" means (09:08–09:20)

headers: Where capability and risk are born
rows: Interpret the task + context (ticket, stack trace, repo).
Decompose into ordered steps (reproduce → locate → patch → verify).
Call real tools (read files, run tests, query logs, call APIs).
A tool = a real permission. This is where capability and risk are born together. [DESIGN-S1 §B]
Make the change, then re-check itself (re-run tests, read the diff).
The only place a human or a gate can stand. [ROS-1.2 §S1]

blocks.text: Key teaching line: The power is the loop. The risk is the tools the loop can touch. [DESIGN-S1 §B]
Visual: a clean 4-node cycle (Reason → Plan → Tool-use → Execute → back to Reason), with a small lock icon on "Tool-use" labeled "permissioned + logged." [DESIGN-S1 §B]

On-slide sharp caption (lands at the 10:12 recap, after the room has a frame — not on the cold open): "Reason + Plan are non-deterministic; Tool-use + Execute are where you re-impose determinism." [ROS-1.2 §S1 ★ ON-SLIDE SHARP, Mid-B3 fix]

Why "non-deterministic" matters (forward hook): repeated runs can vary, so a re-run is not independent verification. S3 explains this as model variance / reliability, not "bias." No current recording or clip is claimed; optional future media must be produced and verified first. [ENRICH-1.1 Theme A] [ROS-1.2 §S1 SAY-ALOUD #2] See §6.
C. Tool groups × banking use cases (09:20–09:34)
Map the tool-groups an agent can call to concrete bank tasks, and tier them by risk. The principle planted here pays off in S2. [DESIGN-S1 §C]

rows: bug fix · write unit tests · secure code review
summarize a ticket · draft a change note
run a pipeline · propose (never auto-approve) a release
check code against a control checklist

blocks.text: [DESIGN-S1 §C] [SCOPE: S1 key topics — tool groups + banking use cases]
Committed use-case shortlist to name aloud: bug fix · unit tests · secure code review · compliance checks · log summarization · root-cause analysis (RCA). [SCOPE: S1]
Principle to plant (pays off in S2): the higher the tier, the more the agent must be read-only by default, and the more a human must approve before any write. [DESIGN-S1 §C]

Depth-in-vote (forced-rank poll, ~30s silent commit) — the expert hook in the first hour: "Rank these tool-groups by which you'd gate FIRST: (a) call external APIs · (b) run tests · (c) read prod logs · (d) read code." The trap: "read prod logs" looks read-only-safe but grants access to secrets, PII, and tokens. Reading is sensitive exposure, not exfiltration by itself; exfiltration requires transmission outside the approved boundary. Classify by blast radius and permitted data flow, not only the read/write verb. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:20, Senior-B1 fix] This is not yet an OWASP exploit; it foreshadows S4 (a leaked secret = [OWASP-LLM-2025: LLM02] Sensitive Information Disclosure surface, taught later). Keep S1 framing as posture, not exploit. [ROS-1.2] [SCOPE: no overclaim]

Demo set-up (still in this block): state the rules of engagement on screen before any demo: repo = SecureBank Mini (synthetic, no real data); mode = agent proposes, instructor approves; every action is logged. [DESIGN-S1 §D]

Defender poll (silent commit, ~20s): "Before it writes anything — what's the ONE thing you'd want logged?" (good answers: the diff · the approver · the test result · the tool calls). This seeds the audit-entry hero shot in the demo and the 6 review questions — the defender commits a prediction about logging before they watch the audit entry appear. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:30, Blue-team-B1 fix]
D. Workflow Walkthrough — the live demo (09:34–09:58)

Demo objective: show a coding agent take a failing golden test on a synthetic banking bug, reason about it, propose a patch, run tests to green, and present a clean diff for human approval — so the "wow" lands AND the control story is visible in the same flow. [DESIGN-S1 §(b)]
The repo (pre-seeded, synthetic)

`` securebank-mini/ src/interest.js # calculateInterest(principal, annualRatePct, days) test/interest.test.js # golden test with known-correct expected values → currently FAILING (RED) AGENT_RULES.md # rules of engagement: read-only first · human-approves-writes · log on CHANGELOG.md ` [DESIGN-S1 §(b)] [SCOPE: SecureBank Mini — calculateInterest()]`
The seeded bug — D1 numbers (BINDING, satang-consistent)

The seeded calculateInterest() is "AI-generated" code that looks plausible but is wrong — it drops the satang (whole-baht truncation instead of round-half-up to 2 decimals). The locked values, identical in S1 and re-cited in S3:

CORRECTION APPLIED (binding): Use buggy 267.00 vs correct 267.13 (raw 267.125). The executable bug is whole-baht truncation: Math.floor(267.125) = 267, displayed as 267.00. The fixed branch keeps ACT/360 and applies deterministic round-half-up to two decimal places, producing 267.13. The gap is 13 satang, and a banker in the room can reproduce it from the prepared inputs. [BUILD_PLAN correction #2] [ROS-1.2 §S1 carried-math fix] [DEMOS_PLAIN_LANGUAGE Demo 1]
Narration (Thai): บั๊กคือ "เราทำสตางค์หาย" (ปัดถ้วนเป็นบาทเต็ม) — ลูกค้าได้ดอกเบี้ยขาดไป 13 สตางค์ต่อรอบ × บัญชีเป็นล้าน; วิธีแก้คือ round-half-up ที่ 2 ทศนิยม → 267.13. [ROS-1.2 §S1]
The ticket handed to the agent (on screen, English)
BUG-4471: "Interest postings are a few satang short on the month-end batch. Finance flagged a reconciliation mismatch. Fix calculateInterest() and prove it with the golden tests." [DESIGN-S1 §(b)]
The choreographed flow (what the room sees)

items: Show the failing test FIRST (truth before AI). Run npm test → RED. Say: "AI didn't find this — our test did. The test is the guardrail." [DESIGN-S1 §(b) step 1]
Hand the agent the ticket in read-only mode. [DESIGN-S1 step 2]
Agent REASONS (on screen): reads interest.js, the failing test, CHANGELOG.md; states the hypothesis: whole-baht truncation instead of round-half-up. [DESIGN-S1 step 3]
Agent PLANS: prints an ordered plan (reproduce → locate → propose patch → re-run golden tests → summarize diff). Pause point: ask the room "Is this plan safe to let it write?" [DESIGN-S1 step 4]
Agent PROPOSES a patch (does NOT auto-apply): replace Math.floor(rawInterest) with deterministic round-half-up to 2 dp; ACT/360 is unchanged. [DESIGN-S1 step 5]

HUMAN APPROVAL GATE (the money moment): instructor reviews the diff and approves before the write lands. "This is the control: nothing is written until I say so." [DESIGN-S1 step 6] [SCOPE: Hard constraints — human approval before write]
Agent EXECUTES + self-verifies: applies the approved patch, re-runs npm test → GREEN (267.13). [DESIGN-S1 step 7]
Agent shows the DIFF + plain-language summary. [DESIGN-S1 step 8]

Agent shows the DEMO AUDIT ROW: what was read · what was proposed · who approved · what was written · test result. It is mutable/resettable in memory and demonstrates linkage only. Production must export the record to access-controlled, tamper-evident logging outside the agent's control. [DESIGN-S1 step 9]

blocks.text: Live UI → bounded recovery walkthrough (delivery resilience)

items: Run the real UI: show the vulnerable interest output 267.00, then the fixed output 267.13 using the same golden case. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:34]
Use validated screenshots if live UI fails. The fallback must match the observed build state; do not substitute an unverified media claim. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:46]

Recovery walkthrough: explain a later green-but-wrong change → human-run git revert → recovery evidence using the timeline slide. Label this an illustrative workflow, not captured runtime proof. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:54]

blocks.text: Why "green-but-wrong" is true (not a trick): a passing test proves the test's assertion, not the code's correctness — an agent can write a test that asserts the buggy behavior. This is exactly why the gate must be a human / structural check, not a re-run. [ROS-1.2 §S1 ↳ DEEPER]

CORRECTION — the revert is a HUMAN-RUN recovery, NOT autonomous action. The git revert is operator-driven and itself logged. Never frame any beat as "the AI rolled back production by itself." [SCOPE: no overclaim] [ROS-1.2 binding-constraint check]
Breadth poll (~3m)
Use log summarization ("200 lines of error log → 3-line root-cause") as a second-task example without claiming an unavailable clip exists. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:58]

Defender poll: "What must never leave the approved boundary?" (answer: sensitive log content). Reading/summarizing is not exfiltration; sending that content outside the approved boundary is. [ROS-1.2 §S1 09:58] [DESIGN-S1 ↳ DEEPER]
Delivery fallback (mandatory — online, ~50 people)

items: Validated static UI set: vulnerable interest result · fixed interest result · approval state · demo audit row. [DESIGN-S1]
Decision rule: attempt the local UI; on failure switch to the matching screenshots and state that they are captured evidence from the same build. [DESIGN-S1]
Pre-seed the repo to a known-good state and rehearse the UI run same-day. [DESIGN-S1]
A captioned recording is an optional future fallback only after it is produced and verified; none is assumed available now.

blocks.text: E. The 6 secure-review questions — "what YOU check" (09:58–10:12)

These are the reviewer-reflex participation hooks — verbal / show-of-hands / chat poll, no hands-on. Framed as what YOU, the reviewer, check before approving any agent change (defender stake). [DESIGN-S1 §(b)] [ROS-1.2 §S1 10:01]

rows: Scope — did it stay in the ticket, or touch files it shouldn't?
Truth source — do we trust the agent's claim, or the golden test?
Logic vs plausibility — the code looked correct; where would a confident-but-wrong fix hide, and what catches it?
Day-count assumption — the agent assumed a basis; who confirms it, the agent or a human + the spec?
Blast radius — if this were transferFunds() not a pure calc, would you let it run the same way?
→ S5; the literal S4 [OWASP-LLM-2025: LLM06] climax
Audit — six months from now, how do we prove who approved this interest-math change?

blocks.text: [DESIGN-S1 §(b) review questions]

Expert feed (mandatory spoken aside, ~20s, whole room) on Q6: "'Could it have lied?' is the question that separates a junior reviewer from a senior one. A test can be GREEN and still wrong — you'll watch that exact thing in the revert beat, and after lunch you'll watch the same prompt give two different confident answers. A passing check is evidence, not proof. The senior reviewer assumes the agent could be confidently wrong and looks for the gate that catches it anyway." [ROS-1.2 §S1 SAY-ALOUD #2, Blue-team-B3 fix]

CORRECTION — agent-review is NOT the gate. Q6 trains skepticism, not a control. "The AI said it's fine" is never an approval gate; the deterministic / human gate stands. This is the agent-review ≠ gate rule, taught explicitly in S5. [ENRICH-1.1 Theme A & B — agent-review is not the approval gate]
F. Map the demo → 4 safe-adoption principles (10:12–10:24)
The four committed safe-adoption principles were demonstrated physically on screen, not merely stated. [DESIGN-S1 §(c)] [SCOPE: S1 — safe adoption]

rows: Agent started read-only (steps 2–3): read code/test/changelog before proposing
Let the agent look before it touches. Most value (triage, review, summaries) needs read-only only.
Agent scoped to the repo + ticket; could not reach CI/CD or prod (Q1, Q5)
Give the agent the smallest set of tools the task needs — nothing more.
The explicit approval gate at step 6 — the patch did not land until approved
AI proposes, a human disposes. Every write/destructive action passes a human gate.
The readable log at step 9 (read → proposed → approved-by → written → result)
If you can't audit it, you can't run it in a bank. Log what was read, proposed, approved, and changed.

blocks.text: [DESIGN-S1 §(c)]

Backdrop standard (say-aloud, optional depth): these four principles align with established AI-governance practice — the NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes responsible AI around Govern · Map · Measure · Manage, and "human-approves-writes + audit-everything" is the operational expression of that posture for a bank. [NIST-AI-RMF] [SCOPE: Reference standards]
Safe-adoption ladder (visual, ascending steps):
Read-only → Least privilege → Human approves writes → Everything audited caption: "Start at the bottom. Earn each step up." [DESIGN-S1 §(c)]
G. Recap + bridge to S2 (10:24–10:30)
Slide key points (English):

items: An agent reasoned, planned, used tools, executed — and a human still decided. [DESIGN-S1 §G]
Speed came with a diff to review and a log to audit — not instead of them. [DESIGN-S1 §G]
Next (S2): turn this posture into a repeatable control — task card → approval gate → execution proof → audit trail. [DESIGN-S1 §G] [ROS-1.2 §S2]

blocks.text: WHY → HOW callback (seeds the S2 open): S1 gives the posture (WHY); S2 gives the mechanism (HOW). Same idea, two altitudes — reinforcement, not repeat. [ROS-1.2 §S2 10:49 callback] [BUILD_PLAN correction relevant to S1↔S2]

Closing framing (Thai): สิ่งที่เห็นวันนี้ไม่ใช่ "AI ขึ้น production เอง" — แต่คือ assisted triage + human approval gate + audit trail. agent เร่งงานให้ (reason/plan/patch/test) แต่ "คนเซ็น" และ "ระบบจดทุกอย่าง" ยังอยู่ครบ. นี่คือรูปแบบเดียวที่ใช้ได้จริงในธนาคาร — และ S2 จะทำให้ guardrail นี้เป็น control ที่ทำซ้ำได้. [DESIGN-S1 §(c)] [SCOPE: Hard constraints]
